messages.subject: debugging transformed data
parts:
I'm creating a large-ish matrix in the transformed data block, and I want to make sure that it is correct. If I use print() statements in the transformed data block, then the large-ish matrix scrolls off the R terminal and is too painful to verify visually. Is there a way to have the print() statements output to a file?

Alternatively, is there a way to tell stan() to save transformed data to the stanfit object, similar to how stan(..., pars=) can save parameter values?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: debugging transformed data
parts:
On Monday, June 3, 2013 4:21:54 PM UTC-4, jacktanner wrote:
I'm creating a large-ish matrix in the transformed data block, and I want to make sure that it is correct. If I use print() statements in the transformed data block, then the large-ish matrix scrolls off the R terminal and is too painful to verify visually. Is there a way to have the print() statements output to a file?

I have a hard time thinking of a case where it would be necessary to do more than verify the first and last rows of the big matrix. And if the matrix has too many columns to easily read, then verifying just the first and last column of the first and last rows ought to be sufficient.

If for some reason that I am currently unable to think of, you really do need to check every single element, I suppose you could create a matrix in the generated quantities block that simply copied the datamatrix. Although then you would have as many "realizations" of the copied matrix as there were post-warmup iterations.

Ben

No, there's not a way to print to a file, nor do we plan to
add such a method any time soon.

How are you going to verify the transformed data is right if it's
printed to a file?

Can you code the verification up programatically in Stan? The transformed
data block only gets executed once, so you should feel free to
carry out some heavy computations. Easy checks would be things
like the matrices being positive or no entries being NaN. Or even
pairs of rows being orthogonal to within some tolerance.

The data type constraints are automatically checked (for instance,
positive-definiteness for a covariance matrix, or being non-negative
and adding up to 1 for a simplex).

I think it'd be helpful to have something like a way to quit
out of Stan gracefully with an error report. Like maybe

exit(...)

with the same arbitrary number of arguments to print as print().

- Bob
